# 1 Enoch Chapter 36 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Watchers

---

**36:1** And from there I went to the south to the ends of the earth, and I saw there three open portals of heaven; and from there come dew and rain and wind.

**36:2** And from there I went to the east to the ends of the heaven, and I saw there the three eastern portals of heaven open and small portals above them.

**36:3** Through each of these small portals pass the stars of heaven and run their course to the west on the path that is shown to them.

**36:4** And as often as I saw these things, I always blessed the Lord of Glory; and I continued to bless the Lord of Glory who has wrought great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of his work to the angels and to human beings, that they might praise his work and all his creatures: that they might see the work of his power and praise the great work of his hands and bless him forever.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering adjudicated from EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic). Chapter 36 concludes the Book of Watchers (chs. 1-36). The southern and eastern portals (vv. 1-3) complete the four-directional survey of heaven's gates. Enoch's closing doxology (v. 4) is the theological capstone of the Book of Watchers: God reveals cosmic wonders so that angels and humans may praise him forever.*
